definitions.explanation: A public appeal or call to action directed at people, asking them to do something. Also refers to the act of addressing or calling out to someone.

examples.japanese: {市民|しみん}への{呼|よ}びかけが{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: An appeal was made to the citizens.

examples.japanese: {節電|せつでん}の{呼|よ}びかけに{応|おう}じる{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: More people responded to the call to save electricity.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{国民|こくみん}に{注意|ちゅうい}の{呼|よ}びかけを{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: The government continues to urge the public to be cautious.

notes:
Derived from the verb {呼|よ}びかける (to call out to, to appeal to). Commonly used in news and official contexts for public appeals or campaigns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{呼|よ}びかけに{応|おう}じる — to respond to an appeal
・{呼|よ}びかけを{行|おこな}う — to make an appeal
・{注意|ちゅうい}の{呼|よ}びかけ — warning call, caution advisory
・{協力|きょうりょく}の{呼|よ}びかけ — call for cooperation
